domain_restrictions: n is an integer and n is at least 1.
Each E_k is a natural number for every k from 0 to n.
The recurrence is assumed only for integers m with 2 <= m <= n.
In the recurrence, j ranges over odd integers with 1 <= j <= m.
The indices j - 1 and m - j must stay within the available range of the sequence, which is ensured by 1 <= j <= m.
The conclusion is only for indices m between 0 and n inclusive.
semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: For any integer n at least 1, any sequence of natural numbers E_0 through E_n with E_0 equal to 1, E_1 equal to 1, and satisfying the given odd-index recurrence for every m from 2 to n must have every term E_m strictly positive for all m from 0 to n.
quantifier_order: Fix an integer n with n at least 1.
Choose natural numbers E_0 through E_n.
Assume E_0 equals 1 and E_1 equals 1.
For every integer m with 2 <= m <= n, define E_m by the stated sum over odd j.
Then for every integer m with 0 <= m <= n, conclude E_m is greater than 0.

variables.name: n
variables.role: fixed upper bound for the sequence and induction range

variables.name: E
variables.role: sequence satisfying the initial conditions and recurrence

variables.name: m
variables.role: index in the recurrence and in the positivity conclusion

witness_dependencies: There is no existential witness in the statement; the only quantified objects are the fixed integer n, the sequence E, and the indices m and j.
The recurrence value of E_m depends on all earlier terms E_{j-1} and E_{m-j} appearing in the sum for that specific m.
The positivity conclusion does not introduce a new witness; it is a universal claim over m.

statement_nl: Fix an integer n with n at least 1. Let E_0,E_1,...,E_n be natural numbers such that E_0 = 1, E_1 = 1, and for every integer m with 2 <= m <= n one has E_m = sum over odd j with 1 <= j <= m of binomial(m-1,j-1) E_{j-1} E_{m-j}. Then E_m > 0 for every integer m with 0 <= m <= n.
